newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tough for Russian oil sector to globalise - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Tough for Russian oil sector to globalise - analyst.

text.p: Russia's move to enter the competitive global oil market is being hampered by a management crisis due to its inability to cope with a market economy, a Russian energy analyst said on Wednesday.

Russia's oil sector is confronted by a growing financial crisis resulting from general mismanagement of the industry through misguided pricing, tax and budget policies, said Eugene M. Khartukov from Moscow's International Centre for Petroleum Studies.
He was presenting a paper at the Asia-Pacific Petroleum Conference (APPEC). Khartukov is also the chief of Moscow's World Energy Analysis and Forecasting Group.

He said that in the absence of a market mentality and the predominance of paternalistic state tendencies, the industry would set and follow its own Eurasian development strategies instead of integrating into the world market.

The most ambitious Russian oil companies, like LUKoil, YUKOS, Rosneft and Tatneft, have ventured with their limited capital in the former Soviet Republics, Eastern Europe, North Africa, the Middle East and Latin America, he said.
LUKoil, YUKOS and Sidanco have also created their own Geneva- and Vienna-based trading arms to penetrate the world oil trade.

"Still, the coming of the Russian majors into the international oil business is greatly hindered by their financial weakness, while their competitiveness vis-a-vis foreign counterparts is seriously undermined by poor economics of Russian oil," Khartukov said.
He said Russian crude oil was underpriced due to the poor state of its refineries, which limit domestic demand.
Even though the government planned to bring domestic crude prices to world levels, an immediate hike to international levels was neither desirable nor possible, he said.
Any rise in Russian crude price against the depressed market value of refinery output would strangle the refining industry which is already on the verge of bankruptcy, he said.
